facts.claim: Master sheet (table_index 0) has a header row at row 1 and 12 data rows in rows 2-13; columns are SKU, Company, Item code, Description. The raw read of A1:D13 shows values in every data cell.
Master.SKU has 12 distinct non-null values across the 12 data rows; examples include TH-0001, MY-0003, and MY-0001. It is unique within this table.
Master.Company contains only TH and MY, six rows each, across rows 2-13.
Master.Item code has six distinct values (0001-0006), each appearing twice because the same item code occurs under both TH and MY. Raw cells preserve leading zeros such as '0001'.
Master.Description has 12 distinct values and mirrors Company plus Item code, e.g. 'TH item 1' and 'MY item 3'.
The composite key (Company, Item code) is unique in Master: 12 rows, 12 distinct combinations, and 0 duplicate keys in the join check.
Stock sheet (table_index 1) has a header at row 1 and 12 data rows in rows 2-13; columns are Company, Item code, Quantity pieces. The raw read of A1:C13 shows values in every data cell.
Stock.Company contains TH and MY, six rows each; Stock.Item code has six distinct code values, each appearing twice, with leading zeros preserved such as '0005'.
Stock.Quantity pieces has 12 distinct integer values across the 12 rows, ranging from 11 to 166: 11, 22, 33, 44, 55, 66, 111, 122, 133, 144, 155, 166.

A full join check on (Company, Item code) between Master and Stock matched all 12 Master rows to all 12 Stock rows with cardinality 1:1, 0 unmatched rows on either side, and 0 duplicate keys in either table.
In all 12 Master rows, SKU text equals Company + '-' + the four-character Item code, e.g. TH + '-' + 0001 gives TH-0001 and MY + '-' + 0003 gives MY-0003.

hypotheses: Stock rows represent one stock quantity per Company+Item code; the workbook does not define an as-of date or stock type.
Master is the intended product population for output because it carries SKU and Description and the operator says the SKU in Master is the output identity.
Description is intended to fill product_name; no separate product-name column exists.
Quantity pieces is already in individual pieces and should not be multiplied by a pack size; no pack-size column exists in either sheet.
The complete 1:1 join in this 12-row file suggests every Master product has a Stock record here, but that does not prove completeness for other exports or periods.
mapping_guidance: Drive output from Master rows 2-13 and emit exactly 12 objects for this file, one per Master.SKU.
Set sku from Master.SKU (A2:A13) as a string; preserve leading zeros and do not derive it numerically from Item code.
Set product_name from Master.Description (D2:D13).
Join Stock to Master on Company and Item code as text, not on Item code alone.
Set qty from matched Stock.Quantity pieces (C2:C13); this file's join is complete 1:1, so all 12 qty values are populated.
If a Master row has no Stock match in another file, set qty to null per the schema; do not default to zero.
Do not emit Stock-only rows; Master defines the product population.
Do not aggregate duplicate Stock rows silently; if duplicates appear, treat the grain as unresolved.
Do not apply unit conversion: the source header says Quantity pieces and the target semantic is stock.qty in individual pieces.
Never match Item code across companies; Company is part of the join key.
The observed SKU format is Company-Item code, but use Master.SKU as authoritative rather than reconstructing SKU from components.
missing_information: No source definition states whether Quantity pieces is on-hand, available, or another stock measure, nor is there an as-of date.
No explicit statement says Master.Description is the product name, although it is the only descriptive field in Master.
No business rule states how to handle future Master rows lacking a Stock match; the target schema allows null qty but does not define the exception policy.
No documented SKU construction rule exists beyond the observed Company-Item code pattern; use existing Master.SKU rather than reconstructing it.
The target has no Company field; company separation must be preserved inside SKU and in the join keys.

changes_from_draft: Added the Stock source and a left join from Master to Stock on Company + Item code, with trim/upper/strip-leading-zero normalization so item codes match without losing company separation.
Mapped /product_name from Master.Description, the only descriptive product field in the master list.
Mapped /qty from Stock.Quantity pieces using parse_number_th; no unit conversion is applied because the source header already declares pieces.
Set record dedupe to /sku with keep=error so future duplicate SKU conflicts are not silently dropped.
Set attributes_passthrough=false because the target schema has additionalProperties=false; Company and Item code are join keys, not output attributes.
Kept /sku directly from Master.SKU to preserve the authoritative identity and leading zeros.
Added quality rules for /sku uniqueness/non-null, /product_name non-null, and a warning when /qty remains null.
